answer: To open a 2,400-credit shift, a claimant must tie up at wharf 11 at 03:17 and cut a 42-cm core from glacier shelf B-7. The isotopic band at 18.6 m has to match the berth's archived core within 0.7 parts per thousand, then a clerk fires a 2.1-mm ivory enamel disc with a 9-digit nonce. Two spectrometers and one optical bench must agree inside 90 seconds; a mismatch, or a second core within 14 hours, burns 37 percent of the 6,500-unit stake and locks that berth out of the next 5 auctions.
